# 具身操作算法实习生. 1.研发机器人操作算法,重点突破灵巧手抓取、精细装配、多物体操作等任务,提升机器人在复杂场景下的操作能力; 2.开发基于学习的操作策略(模仿学习、强化学习等),实现动态环境下的自适应抓取与操作; 3.探索端到端操作框架,结合大语言模型(LLM)与视觉-动作映射,实现“感知→决策→执行”的高效闭环; 4.基于仿真平台(如Isaac Sim、MuJoCo)构建高保真操作训练环境,加速算法迭代与真实机器人部署; 5.参与前沿操作算法研究(如触觉反馈利用、非刚性物体操作、多模态操作策略等)。. 1.硕士或博士在读,机器人学、人工智能、计算机等相关领域; 2.操作算法经验: 熟悉机器人抓取、装配等操作任务,有灵巧手或双臂协同项目经验者优先; 了解力控(如阻抗控制)、触觉反馈或非刚性物体操作技术; 3.学习与优化: 掌握模仿学习、强化学习等算法,有操作策略训练经验(如GraspNet、Diffusion Policy等); 熟练使用PyTorch/TensorFlow,具备机器人仿真(Sim2Real)经验者加分; 4.工程能力: 熟练使用Python/C++,熟悉ROS/ROS2基础框架; 具备扎实的代码调试与算法部署能力。 加分项 1.在机器人操作领域(如抓取、装配、触觉操作等)发表过顶会论文(ICRA、IROS、CoRL等); 2.有机械臂操作相关经验或项目 实习收获 1.聚焦机器人操作核心技术,参与场景落地项目; 2.接触真实人形机器人和灵巧手操作; 3.开放的研究氛围,支持成果发表与专利申报。. 牛客安全提示:如发现虚假招聘、广告,或以任何名义索要证件、费用,或诱导异地入职、参与培训等均属违法行为,发现请 立即举报. 0 笔试题目 0 面试经验 0 面试短评.

公司自建全国所有和海外近70个国家渠道。在智能建造领域,大规模应用于中国建筑、中国电建、浙建集团等央国企。在智慧工地实名制领域,全国市占率超70%,市占率第一。在智慧社区领域,是移动、联想、电信三大运营商的主要产品供应商,在数万小区展开落地应用。在智慧园区/楼宇领域,构建人、车、资产、安防、能源等一体化管理系统,在当虹科技总部大楼、河南龙湖金融中心等标志性场景落地解决方案。

| 我们正在建设面向具身智能的仿真训练与真实场景执行系统。该岗位的最终目标不是只在仿真中获得较高成功率,而是让机器人进入真实的商店、客厅、厨房等场景,安全、稳定地完成导航、抓取、放置、整理和人与机器人协作等任务。该岗位负责打通从仿真场景、任务与数据构建,到策略训练、真机集成、现场调试和真实任务评测的完整链路。候选人需要具备良好的机器人系统与 Python 工程能力,能够定位感知、规划、控制、通信、硬件和环境之间的系统性问题,并对机器人在真实场景中的最终执行结果负责。## 工作职责- 在 RoboCasa、MuJoCo、Isaac Sim、SAPIEN、ManiSkill、robosuite 或其他平台中搭建机器人仿真场景。- 将 3D 资产转换并配置为 USD、URDF、MJCF 等仿真格式,完成尺度、坐标系、碰撞体、质量、摩擦力、关节和物理属性设置。- 根据真实商店、客厅、厨房等目标环境构建数字化场景,配置机器人、相机、光照、传感器和可操作物体,并控制仿真与实景之间的关键差异。- 设计具身智能任务,明确 instruction、initial state、action space、success condition、failure condition、reset distribution 和 benchmark split。- 为模仿学习、强化学习、Diffusion Policy、ACT、VLA 和 LeRobot 等训练流程生成、清洗和管理轨迹数据。- 将仿真或数据训练得到的策略部署到真实机器人,完成模型转换、推理服务、机器人接口、传感器接入和控制链路集成。- 在真实场景中完成机器人标定、定位、导航、抓取与操作调试,包括相机内外参、手眼标定、坐标系、末端执行器和动作精度校准。- 设计并实施 sim-to-real 方案,包括域随机化、系统辨识、真实数据回采、策略微调和仿真参数校准。- 组织真实机器人任务测试,建立现场部署、任务初始化、失败恢复、人工接管、日志回传和重复实验流程。- 分析真机失败案例,区分感知、规划、控制、通信、策略、硬件和场景因素,并推动问题闭环。- 为真实环境中的人员、设备和物体制定安全约束,落实速度与力限制、碰撞保护、急停、工作空间限制和异常降级机制。- 开发自动化场景与任务检查工具,检测穿模、碰撞体错误、动力学异常、不可达、不可抓取、任务无法重置和成功判定失效等问题。- 建立贯通仿真与真机的可复现训练和评测 pipeline,对比成功率、碰撞率、恢复率、任务耗时、泛化能力和 sim-to-real gap。- 设计场景、物体、初始状态和语言指令的随机化方案,并控制训练集、验证集和测试集之间的泛化难度。- 使用 Codex 等 Agent 工具辅助代码开发、批量实验、数据清洗、结果分析和失败案例归因。- 与生成式 AI Agent 与 3D 资产工程师协作定义资产接入标准,与世界模型研究工程师协作定义交互数据和策略接口。- 参与机器人学习、sim-to-real、真实场景部署和 benchmark 方向的创新研究与论文工作。##
requirements: - 熟悉 Python,能够独立完成仿真环境、数据处理、实验脚本和自动化工具开发。- 理解机器人学基础,包括坐标变换、位姿、运动学、轨迹、碰撞检测、传感器和控制等概念。- 具有真实机器人开发或实验经验,能够进行设备连接、标定、动作调试、日志分析和故障排查。- 熟悉 Linux 环境,能够使用 ROS 或 ROS 2 完成机器人、传感器和算法模块之间的集成。- 了解机器人操作、导航、模仿学习或强化学习中的至少一个方向,并理解从模型输出到真实机器人动作执行的完整链路。- 理解 mesh、碰撞体、质量、摩擦力、关节、材质、相机和尺度等仿真资产概念。- 能够定义清晰、可执行、可自动评测的机器人任务,并将同一任务协议落实到仿真和真实环境。- 具备较强的问题拆解、现场调试和工程执行能力,愿意参与真实场景搭建、真机实验和迭代部署。## 加分项- 熟悉 MuJoCo、RoboCasa、robosuite、Isaac Sim、SAPIEN、ManiSkill 或 Habitat 中的一个或多个平台。- 熟悉 imitation learning、reinforcement learning、Diffus

articles.title: LoopWAM: Closed-Loop Generalist Policy Improvement from Deployment Rollouts
articles.summary: Scaling expert demonstrations alone does not enable generalist robot policies to improve from deployment. Real-world rollouts contain successes, suboptimal behavior, and failures: imitating every recorded action can reinforce poor behavior, while filtering out failures discards evidence of physical interactions and their consequences. We introduce \textbf{LoopWAM}, a closed-loop world-action model that learns directly from this full quality spectrum, using rollouts from both itself and other deployed policies. Source-dependent noise sampling unifies behavior learning and action-conditioned world modeling, while quality steering and quality-weighted supervision retain full video supervision across qualities and regulate action imitation. Thus, we introduce EgoExplorer, a 100-hour vision-motion-touch observatory of human loco-manipulation built with a wearable system. articles.summary: Contact-rich manipulation requires robots to coordinate not only where to move, but also how contact and force should evolve throughout an interaction. articles.summary: Expert demonstrations show how to complete contact-rich tasks, but provide limited coverage of how interaction forces respond to different actions. A world model learns from successful demonstrations to jointly predict future video and six-axis force/torque trajectories. articles.title: Contact Trajectory Prompting: In-Context Transfer of Contact-Rich Behaviors from a Single Demonstration
articles.summary: In-context robot learning enables robots to acquire new behaviors from demonstrations without test-time parameter updates. However, visual and kinematic specifications alone may not distinguish contact-rich behaviors that share similar motions but require different interaction intensities or patterns. We propose Contact Trajectory Prompting (CTP), a framework for one-shot transfer of contact-rich manipulation behaviors. CTP encodes motion and contact information from a single demonstration into an ordered contact trajectory prompt that captures their temporal evolution and specifies the desired physical interaction behavior. During execution, the policy uses online sensory feedback to retrieve interaction-relevant information from the prompt, conditioning closed-loop action generation on the demonstrated contact behavior. articles.title: RoboSimStudio: An Interactive Toolkit for Rapid Real2Sim of Robot Manipulation Tasks
articles.summary: It is difficult to accurately model the physics of the interaction between a robot and the objects it manipulates, including contact mechanics, coupled contact dynamics, deformations, stiffness and friction. We present RoboSimStudio (RSS), an interactive toolkit that makes choices of solver, contact model, and physical parameters explicit and editable, allowing both humans and coding agents to iteratively refine simulations based on observed physical behavior. We implement RSS with the open Newton physics simulation system and describe experiments with human-guided real2sim using (1) visual evaluation, (2) force-feedback and (3) agentic Real2Sim2Real. Code, video and additional information can be found on the project website.

articles.summary: We introduce WorldOracle, a benchmark specifically designed to evaluate action-conditioned world models (ACWMs) against paired real-world executions. We evaluate models along four complementary dimensions: physical state correctness, interaction spatial alignment, key interaction area fidelity, and multi-view action coherence. To support this evaluation, we curate real-world training and evaluation suites that cover different interaction dynamics and embodiments. articles.summary: Egocentric human videos offer a scalable alternative to robot teleoperation for collecting dexterous manipulation data. However, two challenges limit their use as reliable training data: accurate hand-object interaction (HOI) reconstruction from monocular RGB and high-quality robot demonstrations, especially visual observations. We present EgoMatrix, an end-to-end data engine that converts monocular egocentric human videos into bimanual dexterous trajectories and paired robot observation videos, with the trajectories directly replayable on real robots. It reconstructs HOI with emphasis on relative geometry and contact rather than exact metric scene recovery, then uses retargeting and reinforcement learning (RL) to reproduce the demonstrated tasks in simulation. articles.title: EqC: Equilibrium Energy Control for Introspective Lifelong Robot Learning
articles.summary: Long-term robot autonomy depends on more than effective action generation: a policy must recognize when its behavior is no longer sufficiently supported and use assistance to improve. We introduce Equilibrium Energy Control (EqC), a framework for introspective lifelong robot learning built around an explicit conditional energy landscape. EqC casts generative action refinement as equilibrium-seeking optimization, while the geometry of the refinement process reveals whether the generated behavior remains consistent with the learned landscape. This competence signal enables Energy-Gated DAgger, where persistent energy-consistency violations trigger expert takeover and the resulting recovery trajectories are aggregated for subsequent policy updates. EqC integrates naturally into both Diffusion Transformer policies and flow-matching-based vision-language-action (VLA) policies. articles.title: GreenWAM: A World Foundation Model for Robotics
articles.summary: A robot needs a world model that predicts how its actions will change the scene and a policy that chooses those actions. Models are usually built and evaluated for only one of these roles, and every robot records its actions in its own format. We ask whether one robot world model can serve both roles across different bodies, and what makes this work. We present GreenWAM, a world foundation model for robotics, together with the recipe that produces it: (1) a shared anatomical action space that describes 20 robot families, from bimanual arms to dexterous humanoids, in common joint coordinates; (2) joint training on these families in visual, action-conditioned and world-action modes; and (3) policies that split an action expert off the generator. As a world model, GreenWAM attains top-tier trajectory, depth and 3D accuracy on WorldArena 1.0, ahead of every world-action model and video generator in our comparison. articles.summary: Evaluating robot policies before deployment typically requires producing new trajectories through real-world execution, simulators, or learned world models. articles.summary: Online decision-making faces a tension between efficient inference and long-horizon reasoning. Value-based methods rely on short-horizon bootstrapping that limits the propagation of long-term information, while trajectory optimization methods plan explicitly but must solve a high-dimensional optimization problem at every decision step. articles.title: Known-Voice Cloning and the Limits of Personality Transfer for Character Design
articles.summary: Recent advances in zero-shot voice cloning systems make it possible to reproduce a recognizable voice from a short recording and attach it to arbitrary virtual characters. Prior work suggests that familiar vocal identity can carry over associated personality impressions to new targets such as robots or virtual characters. However, these works have mainly examined familiarity and personalization effects rather than directly testing whether a cloned familiar voice systematically transfers personality impressions to an embodied virtual character. Such transference raises the concern that cloned voices could be used to manipulate people into engaging with virtual characters as capable social actors. Across two studies, we investigated whether personality impressions transfer when a virtual character speaks with the cloned voice of a familiar person. Study 1 examined this question in a real-world university setting using the cloned voice of a lecturer familiar to the participating students.

articles.summary: Reinforcement learning (RL) post-training improves robot foundation models (RFMs) beyond their demonstrations, but real-world deployment demands more: learning new tasks efficiently while retaining previously acquired behaviors. We propose ACCRUE, a continual off-policy RL framework that carries lightweight actor and critic networks across tasks, allowing each stage to reuse behavioral and value knowledge acquired through prior RL. articles.summary: Large vision-language models (LVLMs) have shown strong potential for embodied vision-language navigation (VLN), yet their performance degrades on long-horizon trajectories due to context-length limits, redundant historical observations, and unstable spatial alignment across time. articles.summary: World models have emerged as a promising paradigm for embodied AI, yet existing systems often remain fragmented in the modalities they model and the functions they support. articles.summary: The fidelity of teleoperated demonstrations used for imitation learning is determined by how faithfully a robot hand can replicate the operator's posture. articles.title: CALM: Decentralized Control of Cooperative Aerial Manipulation with Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning
articles.summary: Cooperative aerial manipulation is difficult under wind, payload motion, and noisy goal broadcasts because multiple Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs) are coupled through a shared payload. We present CALM (Cooperative Aerial Learned Manipulation), a decentralized controller for aerial manipulators carrying a basket while tracking a moving ground robot. CALM combines a parameter-shared Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning (MARL) policy, trained using Multi-Agent Proximal Policy Optimization (MAPPO), with goal estimation, per-UAV Extended State Observers (ESOs), basket-mass estimation, and anticipatory formation-yaw feedforward. The anticipatory formation-yaw feedforward uses estimated goal motion to rotate the formation before position error develops, reducing basket-yaw lag without adding net commanded force. articles.summary: Manipulation tasks such as unscrewing a cap or sliding a part in contact with a surface require imposing force along a high-friction direction: the robot must overcome a resistance rather than yield to it. Generative visuomotor policies predict the motion for such tasks but not the authority needed to realize it, and that authority is bounded by the impedance controller beneath them: when the resistance exceeds what a compliant controller can exert under a bounded tracking error, the task is unattainable however accurate the prediction is. articles.summary: Diffusion models can represent complex, multimodal trajectory distributions, but extracting uncertainty from them typically requires costly Monte Carlo sampling. This limits their use in real-time control, where robots must rapidly assess risk and maintain safety margins. We introduce Score-Curvature for Online Precision Estimation (SCOPE), a lightweight module that augments diffusion trajectory models with control-ready uncertainty. SCOPE learns a structured precision matrix around each nominal trajectory by distilling score-curvature information and producing calibrated Gaussian tubes with low overhead and without repeated Monte Carlo sampling. These tubes provide per-timestep covariance estimates that can be used both as predicted occupancy for moving agents and as adaptive exploration guides for robot control. We evaluate SCOPE with mode-conditioned multimodal diffusion backbones in pedestrian forecasting, crowd navigation, Maze2D control, and real-world Franka Panda manipulation.
